findings.title: PPSW1 recomputes the 6x6 double-double tableau on every step attempt: 80% of its per-step cost
findings.claim: stage_inputs_unchecked calls tableau(sigma) on every attempt (ppsw1.rs:408). tableau builds V, V^-1 (Gauss-Jordan in double-double, :137-165) and 12 double-double 6x6 products (:241-263) with fma through a libm call. It depends only on sigma, which the controller holds at exactly 1.0 for most steps (:946-952), and it is a degree-5 polynomial in sigma, so it can be precomputed once per session. The premise that Vec allocation in ParallelExecution::map_ordered explains the 1-thread cost is wrong: with threads==1 map_ordered is never called (ppsw1.rs:492, :587).
findings.evidence: callgrind, one PeerOde solve of Oregonator n=3 tol 1e-6 (3341 attempts, 661860264 Ir): ppsw1::tableau inclusive 79.87% = 158215 Ir/attempt; solve_stages 12.20% (LuFactorization::solve 7.10%, ::new 1.92%); __rust_alloc+__rust_dealloc 5.47%; starter+h0 rule+output 0.19%. perf stat: PPSW1 197907 instr/attempt vs RODAS5P 13357 (14.8x); standalone tableau 158418 instr/call, 76771 cycles/call; without it PPSW1 would be 3.0x. valgrind: 61.0 heap allocations per PPSW1 attempt vs 0.06 for RODAS5P. Allocation sites: ppsw1.rs:413-427 (12 Vec), selection.rs:881 (n*n), ppsw1.rs:470 (n*n), matrix.rs:259 to_faer + faer LU, ppsw1.rs:478-487 (7), matrix.rs:332-336 (3-4 per solve x6), problem.rs:571 (6), ppsw1.rs:797/:872 (1), selection.rs:1024 (1). JVP provider adds problem.rs:858-875: 3 Vec and n JVP callbacks per step.
findings.impact: Limits scope, does not invalidate HOLD: the U11 G0 step criterion fails on its own (matched-error step ratio 1.91-7.11 against <=1.2). It does invalidate the U11 per-step wall ratios (7.8-24.4x at n=3,8) and speed_vs_production values as method-level numbers: four fifths of the PPSW1 step time is one avoidable function. V10 'equal implementation level' cannot be met before this is removed.
findings.minimal_fix: In a new opt-in session type (ppsw1.rs is not protected, but keep the default path bit-identical): cache the last (sigma, Tableau) pair, or precompute the six sigma-coefficient matrices of B, A, Gamma once and evaluate by Horner; verify bitwise equality of Tableau against tableau(sigma) for the sigma values of a recorded run before using it in V10.
findings.reproduce_cmd: valgrind --tool=callgrind <probe> time ppsw1_t1 1 1e-6 && callgrind_annotate --inclusive=yes callgrind.out.* | grep -E 'tableau|solve_stages|try_step'   # probe source embedded in this file under probe_sources

findings.title: PeerOde returns success=true with an error 1e6-1e7 times the tolerance: the starter interval has no error control
findings.claim: ppsw1::start integrates [t0, t0+2*h0] with one 5-stage Radau IIA step and no error estimate (ppsw1.rs:1125-1256); h0 = min(h_max, 1/||J||_inf) (ppsw1.rs:1023-1035, selection.rs:959-979) ignores rtol/atol and any time scale of f(t, .). When 2*h0 reaches the span (selection.rs:959 caps h0 at half the span), the whole solve is that single step: zero Peer steps, success == true (selection.rs:1028). Option h0 = NaN is silently replaced by the cap (f64::min at :961).
findings.evidence: Executed probe p3: y' = 20 cos(20 t), dense Jacobian 0, span (0,1), rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8 -> success=True, accepted Peer steps=0, y_end=9.226167329988417, exact sin(20)=0.9129452507276277, |error|=8.313. p3b (200 cos 200 t): y_end=-51.118572291016626, |error|=50.25, success=True. p5b: h0=NaN -> success=True, h0 used 5e-1.
findings.impact: Correctness defect of the U07 adapter that the registry admits as ScopedCalibration without admit_unqualified. U11 HOLD is not affected (autonomous problems, h0 <= t_end/100). It limits every matched-error PPSW1 number: the achieved error of a run contains an uncontrolled starter contribution, which V10 must separate or bound. V03 must not copy this adapter pattern unchanged.
findings.minimal_fix: Opt-in adapter change (selection.rs is not protected): reject non-finite or non-positive options.h0; estimate the starter error (for example compare the Radau step against two half steps or use the PPSW1 estimator on the first Peer step with rejection shrinking h0) and refuse or shrink h0 when it exceeds the tolerance; report zero-Peer-step solves as a distinct outcome.
findings.reproduce_cmd: <probe> peer | grep p3   # probe source embedded under probe_sources

findings.title: MethodRegistry admission and GeneralOde::select disagree in both directions (9 executed cases)
findings.claim: The plan states that the registry is not used for routing; executed cases show it also cannot reproduce select. Constraints that select (selection.rs:176-227) and Rodas5p::capabilities (capabilities.rs:66-141) enforce and descriptors/MethodRequest lack: (1) regime (Unknown/Nonstiff -> DOPRI5 only); (2) band storage exemption from max_dense_dimension (:214-220; the rodas5p descriptor has no banded variant, :532-551); (3) the provider form actually present (from_problem_and_policy grants finite_difference for any provider, :311-314, so a JVP problem is admitted as 'finite-difference-dense'); (4) MatrixFreeNotEnabled as a route property; (5) MissingTimeDerivative for ProvidedOnly non-autonomous problems; (6) Options: vector atol refusals, dense_output, InteriorError::Enforce; (7) events require dense output; (8) select refuses mass, events and dense output outright while the rodas5p descriptor advertises all three; (9) Dense provider with declared band counted as dense. Variant labels also differ from the executed route (banded n=10 is admitted as 'explicit-jacobian-dense', route BandedFast).
findings.evidence: Executed probe 'select' (rows in raw_evidence.registry_vs_select): c01 banded provider n=1000: select Ok(Rodas5p, BandedFast), registry Refused(Permission x3); c02 FD + declared band n=1000: same split; c03 JVP n=3 AllowFiniteDifference without matrix-free: select Err(MatrixFreeNotEnabled), registry Admitted 'finite-difference-dense'; c04 non-autonomous ProvidedOnly: select Err(MissingTimeDerivative), registry Admitted; c05 events: select Err(Events), capabilities Err(EventsWithoutDenseOutput), registry Admitted; c06 mass, c08 dense output: select Err, registry Admitted; c07 regime Unknown: select Dopri5, registry admits both; c09 vector atol on JVP: select Err(Implicit(VectorAtolOnMatrixFreeRoute)), registry Admitted 'jvp-matrix-free'. No test compares the two: tests/unified_method_capabilities.rs:243 discards the query result.
findings.impact: Limits scope of U06 ('unified capability registry') to a descriptive table. The V03 discriminator 'registry is the only routing authority and the 1024-combination selection table is identical' is unreachable with the current MethodRequest/descriptor schema.
findings.minimal_fix: Before V03 routing: extend the request with regime, dimension, declared band, provider form, autonomy/time-derivative, atol kind, interior-error mode; add banded and sequential-dense variants to the rodas5p descriptor; add a contract test asserting select == registry-derived selection over the full combination table.
findings.reproduce_cmd: <probe> select   # 13 JSON rows; source embedded under probe_sources

findings.title: PeerOde: permission bypass, untyped and replaced failure reasons, failure without a reason
findings.claim: (a) PeerOde::admission checks only the caller's CapabilitySet, never the provider form (selection.rs:851-864); lower() then uses whatever the problem has (:876-898). (b) success is 'failure.is_none() && t == t_end' (:1028); when the starter endpoint t0 + 2*h0 rounds above t_end the loop is skipped and the result is success=false with failure=None. (c) callback_to_core (:837-847) maps Recoverable to CoreError::NonFinite and Fatal to CoreError::InvalidInput; try_step turns every NonFinite into a halving rejection (ppsw1.rs:786-794) although the Jacobian is re-evaluated at the same (t_m, y_m), so the run ends with an unrelated reason. (d) failure is an Option<String> of a Debug rendering (:815, :966, :985, :1018), not a typed reason. (e) a declared band is admitted by the registry and refused afterwards by lower() (:870).
findings.evidence: Executed probe 'peer': p1 JVP provider with allowed={explicit_jacobian,dense_matrix,newton} -> admission variant 'explicit-jacobian-dense', user JVP callbacks=4, success=True; p2a span (0.3,0.9), zero Jacobian -> success=False, failure=None, t_last=0.9000000000000001; p4 Jacobian returning Recoverable('user says shrink') from the first Peer step -> rejected=52, Jacobian callbacks=54, failure='t=2: InvalidInput("PPSW1 requires a finite, representably advancing time")'; p6 Fatal RHS -> failure='t=2: InvalidInput("fatal callback error: user fatal")'; p7 declared band -> admission Admitted, solve Err(UnsupportedJacobian).
findings.impact: Limits scope of the U07 claims 'typed refusal before callbacks' and 'capability constraint': a caller that forbids JVPs still gets JVP callbacks. No recorded verdict depends on it. Blocks reuse of this adapter as the V03 template for typed fallback.
findings.minimal_fix: Derive the required variant from problem.jacobian and admit that variant; make failure an enum carrying the original CallbackError; treat a Recoverable Jacobian/starter error as a stop with that reason; land the endpoint by setting t = t_end when hh == t_end - t and define success by the landing flag.
findings.reproduce_cmd: <probe> peer   # rows p1, p2a, p4, p6, p7

findings.claim: Read-only review of 93392249. unified/router.rs:63-75 sends Tier2MatrixFreeKrylov, Tier3Exponential, Tier4StagedRodas5p and TierProtectedReference to the same dispatch_rodas5p_tier -> Rodas5p::solve (:193); only the string differs (:175-180). Doc claims without code behind them: router.rs:3-5 ('matrix-free Krylov, L^8=0 staged sweep'); analyzer.rs:15-21 ('staged GMRES with subspace recycling', 'Fused exponential / Leja', 'Staged vectorized L^8=0 causal sweep'); a JVP problem with n<16 is labelled TierProtectedReference 'direct-LU reference driver' (analyzer.rs:121-125) while Rodas5p::solve runs its matrix-free route; mod.rs:3-9 ('Nilpotent homotopy sweep', 'GCRO-DR', 'Newton-Raphson-Free Homotopy / Exponential Actions', 'Zero-Allocation Hot Loops'); options.rs:25-36 and :47-52: profile, max_krylov_restarts and invariant_drift_tol are never read, max_krylov_dim only sizes an unused buffer; workspace.rs:15-30 buffers are never passed to a driver and step_into (:123-144) is a Heun step, yet it carries the VG-1 zero-allocation claim; solution.rs:37 documents max_t |I(y(t)) - I(y0)| while router.rs:316-329 computes the endpoint difference only (fallback.rs:63-68 from the checkpoint, not y0). registry.rs:874/:897: PexprbWindowDriver records method Rodas5p and wraps its counters in Rodas5p stats. tests/unified_production_solver_contracts.rs:232 asserts the label string, not the driver.

Work dropped: router.rs:267-273 copies 7 of the switching counters (factorizations, iterations, attempts, segments, discarded-pilot detail lost) and :277 leaves stats.accepted_steps/attempts at 0; fallback.rs:46 '?' returns the error and drops the charged explicit prefix and route_history; fallback.rs:56 stats.accepted_steps/attempts cover only the fallback leg and inner_solution holds only that leg; registry.rs:296, :548 and :857 work_units omits factorizations. Silent or uncharged: analyzer.rs:113-116 one RHS, :162-172 one dense Jacobian plus an O(n^3) eigen solve at preflight, none charged; router.rs:260-263 escalates to DerivativeFallback::AllowFiniteDifference without a user permission; fallback.rs:44-46 restarts the full max_steps budget; router.rs:222-235 'fall back to protected direct solve' calls the identical Rodas5p::solve(problem, ...) on the same JVP problem, so it is a repeat, not a different route; hybrid_automaton.rs:315-320 accounting_complete() compares a sum with the same sum and is always true. registry.rs SolverState/next_solver_state and HybridRouteAutomaton have no caller in src (the module doc says so).
findings.evidence: File:line reading of commit 933922495045796c99c530b0f1f1efd8fec83ed0 at /home/cosmosapjw/vigilode (not executed: building there is outside this task). grep -rn 'next_solver_state\|HybridRouteAutomaton' crates/vigilode/src returns only registry.rs, hybrid_automaton.rs, lib.rs re-exports and doc comments.
findings.impact: Limits scope: the switcher's claims 'fail-closed', 'strictly conserving all accumulated WorkCounters' (fallback.rs:3-5) and 'complete work accounting' hold only on the success path of SwitchingSolver itself, not for the unified wrapper. Counter-based evidence produced through VigilODE::solve under-reports work. Relevant to the V03 plan to reuse WindowDriver as the execution layer: it needs a typed error first.

findings.title: Switcher preflight classifies contractive (for example diffusion) problems as non-stiff and allocates n*n for every problem
findings.claim: analyzer.rs:174-187 sets is_contracting = mu2(J(t0,y0)) <= 0 with mu2 = lambda_max((J+J^T)/2) (rodas5p-core nonnormal_observers.rs:313) and routes contracting problems with span <= 100 to DOPRI5, reporting is_stiff = !is_contracting (:191). Contractivity is not non-stiffness: every symmetric negative definite Jacobian (heat equation, y' = -1e6 y) has mu2 < 0 and is the standard stiff case. Such a run spends DOPRI5 attempts up to Options::max_steps (default 100000, options.rs:131) before the fallback at router.rs:124-146. analyzer.rs:210-221 sends every finite-difference problem with n <= 10 to DOPRI5 first (Robertson included). unified/workspace.rs:47 allocates vec![0.0; n*n] and :46 (m+1)*n in VigilODE::solve (mod.rs:47) for every problem, including matrix-free ones: n = 1e5 requests 80 GB, n = 1e6 8 TB, before any integration.
findings.evidence: File:line reading; mu2 definition from the observer source. Hand check: J = diag(-1e6) gives mu2 = -1e6 <= 0, span 100 -> Tier1Explicit; DOPRI5 stability limit h <= about 3.3e-6 needs about 3e7 steps > 100000.
findings.impact: Limits scope of the switcher's 'proactive stiffness detection' claim (mod.rs:7) and of any switcher benchmark on MOL problems routed through VigilODE::solve with a dense Jacobian; blocks the large-n regimes that loop L1 targets (V04, V11) through this frontend. No recorded verdict in the unification branch depends on it.
findings.minimal_fix: Do not adopt PreflightAnalyzer as a router. If a stiffness screen is wanted use a spectral-radius times span estimate, charged, with a preregistered threshold; size the workspace lazily per route.

findings.title: PPSW1 6-thread arm: two rayon pool round trips per attempt and a pool built inside the timed solve
findings.claim: With threads > 1 every attempt runs pool.install twice (ppsw1.rs:502 solves, :597 RHS; parallel.rs:62-63) and PeerOde::solve builds a new rayon pool per call (selection.rs:945). The parallelised work at n=3..8 is about 6 solves and 6 RHS (LuFactorization::solve 14063 Ir per attempt), far below one wake/join.
findings.evidence: Recorded U11 rows, recomputed: t6/t1 wall 1.59-2.94; per attempt t1 [17.23, 17.68] us vs t6 [46.28, 49.19] us (Oregonator), [19.64, 21.74] vs [50.66, 63.73] (HIRES). perf cycles:u of the rerun: main thread 72.15%, the six rayon workers 27.85%.
findings.impact: Confirms plan 1.2(a): G0 speed judged on the 6-thread arm at n <= 64 measures thread wake-up, not the method. Does not change HOLD.
findings.minimal_fix: For V10 use the 1-thread arm at small n and a persistent pool with one fork-join per step (solve and RHS fused) where threads are tested.
